results.references: - Peter Richtárik and Hanmin Li. [A Sharper Theory of Ball-Proximal Optimization: Convergence and Radius Selection](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35147v1). 2026, preprint v1 (28 September). Complexity: $O\!\left(\left\lceil\min\left\{R^2/t^2,(R/t)\log(\Delta/\varepsilon),(R/t)\sqrt{\log(\Delta/\varepsilon)}\right\}\right\rceil\right)$ fixed exact ball-minimization oracle calls by the ball-proximal point method for $f(x_K)-f_\star\le\varepsilon$, when $0<\varepsilon<\Delta$; zero calls suffice when $\varepsilon\ge\Delta$ or $R=0$.

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize f over a convex feasible set C. The restricted epigraph {(x,a): x∈C, f(x)≤a} is closed. A minimizer xstar∈C exists; no smoothness or strong convexity is assumed.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexBallProximal.lean: spec.admissible, ConvexOn, IsClosed, and IsMinOn clauses.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact ball-minimization oracle: at any feasible query x, returns y∈argmin{f(z): z∈C, ‖z−x‖≤t}. The reply contains only y. Every call index and seed must satisfy this exact condition; no oracle error or independence assumption is imposed.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexBallProximal.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible oracle-answer clause.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with balls defined by its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E, t, R, Δ, ε, and x0 are public, with t>0, R≥0, Δ>0, and ε>0. C and f are hidden. The feasible start has a common minimizing witness xstar satisfying ‖x0−xstar‖≤R and f(x0)−f(xstar)≤Δ.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexBallProximal.lean: Public, Instance, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible initialization clause.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point must lie in C and satisfy f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for a global minimizer xstar∈C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap guarantee hold almost surely under the joint algorithm/oracle seed law, after execution with a fixed oracle-call budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConvexBallProximal.lean: spec.successful, ∀ᵐ clause; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and execute.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: Convex minimization uses an exact local ball-minimization primitive that solves an entire constrained subproblem per call, an unusual oracle model compared with standard first-order benchmarks.
